videos.script: Some lambdas do nothing but call one method and pass their arguments along. {{same}} s arrow s dot toUpperCase. x arrow Integer dot parseInt of x. Java lets you name the method instead, with two colons, and the result is the same object a lambda would have made. {{kinds}} There are four kinds, and three of them read the same way. The fourth is the one people get wrong. String colon colon length takes its string from the argument. A variable colon colon length has already chosen its string. {{bound}} You will see the difference in one run, where the two print four and twenty-nine. {{ctor}} Constructors have references too, and they turn a class into a supplier or a function. {{close}} And at the end, the case where the compiler cannot tell which method you meant, and refuses.
